title: Assembling the Oliver band and hiring Lil Hardin
summary: For the Royal Garden he recruited Joe Oliver, Johnny Dodds, Mutt Carey, Norah, Minor Hall, and borrowed pianist Lil Hardin from Mrs. Jones's music store.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Royal Garden. And he wants some music, you know. Well, I said, it's a good chance for us to get our old band together. I said, yeah, I'll send for Joe Oliver. Can you get him? I said, sure, I can get him. All right, I'll send for Joe Oliver. That's Joe Oliver. Johnny Dodds come in with Mac and Mac. Over to this little old theater. They had a little old theater there on State Street. It's your big time, you know. He was in there.
Mutt was living for a while too. Mac was there.

I mean, Mutt was there. Yeah. Yeah. I still, I still, uh, may share. And Mutt said, I said, Mutt, I can get you John too. Mutt said, well, I'll go far to St. Louis and I'll jump at St. Louis. He left with St. Louis, but, oh, Bessier just left right away. Well, he played up the deluxe with me. He decided, what's doing? Mutt come back. See? Well, I got Mutt with me. Johnny was very sick, you know. He was sick, you know. I was there. He stayed with me. Then I got Joe. Finally, Nora Dutrae comes through town. He's running a ship. You know, a sailor. Used to come in, you know, and come and sit in and play. So he's telling us about his time was going to go. He'd be off. Be out in the Navy. Nora got out the Navy. We got Nora. Then finally, Minor Hall come in town. Running on the Southern Pacific. Dishwasher over. Why didn't he? He come in town. His mother would live in Chicago and his brother, Tubby. He went to the Army. No, he didn't. No, we got him before he went to the Army. Yeah. He come in town. We got a hold of him. Then we organized our regular bunch. So that name, and I got a girl named Lil Harden. It's the name of Lil Armstrong. She was working for Mrs. Jones, selling music and demonstrating it to the people, you know. And I needed a piano player. I was going to play on the west side for the Chinese, George, you know, at a cafe. But they wanted piano. I had Louis playing guitar. Louis Kaplan. Yeah. So I said, I'm going to get this girl. You know, she could play. I know she could play. So I asked her, I said, I would like to play a job. You want to play a gig tonight with her? Yeah, I'll play with you. I said, brother, you know. I don't know what it's paid. I'll play. She just wanted to be with the jazz. Say she was in a jazz band. That's the only jazz band. So she said, you ask Mrs. Jones. I said, Mrs. Jones, can I use your piano player? Now listen. Listen, you come in here to steal. I said, steal your piano player. I just want to use it tonight. All right. We started the monkey business. I said, how can it be monkey business? I ain't got no regular job. I'm just going down there to play this gig. All right. She can go. Okay. We went down there to Charmin hard the band. She liked the band. And she was, oh, you know how old she was? 17 years old. That's old. That's right. I put her in a place of band. And I went down there and play and she used to go home. And I said, well, where are you? Where are you at all the time? Well, she was playing down at the church. She lied to her mother for years. Said she was at some church.
She was playing at some church. She was playing at the...

And we all got together playing in the dreamlands. She still thought she was playing at some church or something. And her mother come and they caught her. Too late then. And Miss Jones gave me the devil. I said, I know you're going to steal my girl. I didn't. Soon she went out. I know that was the last of it. She went down and played that day and didn't go back tomorrow. Called Miss Jones up and said, I got a regular job with that band.
And I'm going to live this woman's house. I live at Miss Jones's house.
She said, I know you're going to do that, you devil. And she's crazy about the band, on the old man's boat. Right.
